title: Integrated OKR Map + Initiative Boundary Playbook
creator: Priya Patel
body:
Purpose:
Create a single, repeatable playbook and deliverable (Integrated OKR Map) that ties company-level objectives to cross-functional initiatives, defines initiative boundaries, and enforces a lightweight RACI and dependency grid for each planning cycle. The goal is to reduce ambiguity during quarterly planning, speed up handoffs, and ensure initiatives map clearly to measurable OKR outcomes.

Scope:
- Company-level objectives (North Star + three supporting objectives) mapped to specific initiatives owned by Eng/Product/Design/Sales/Security.
- Initiative boundary template (what is in/out, success criteria, metrics, rollout plan).
- Dependency grid and escalation path for inter-team work.
- Lightweight gating criteria for moving an initiative between Backlog -> Planned -> In Progress -> Done for the cycle.
- Integration with existing artifacts: Roadmap board (Linear), Initiative PRDs (Confluence), Implementation trackers (GitHub), and console analytics dashboards.

Deliverables:
- Integrated OKR Map (spreadsheet + canonical Confluence page) using the initiative boundary template.
- Initiative Dependency Grid (CSV) exported into the roadmap board with dependencies linked to Linear keys.
- Playbook: step-by-step checklist for PMs and Eng leads for cycle planning and mid-cycle rebinds.

Initiative Boundary Template (required fields):
1) Initiative Key (Linear) and short title
2) Owner (team + person)
3) In-scope items (bulleted)
4) Out-of-scope items (bulleted)
5) Success metrics (OKR metric linkage, target delta)
6) Rollout plan & rollout tags (canary, immediate, opt-in)
7) Critical dependencies (Linear keys / GitHub PRs / infra tickets)
8) Risk & mitigation summary
9) Post-release observability plan (dashboards/alerts)

Mapping format and example: each company objective row will include a linked list of initiatives with initiative boundaries summarized. Example (abbreviated):
- Objective: Reduce cost per token 25% without QoL regressions
  - Initiative: ENG-2062 "Batching & kernel selection improvements" (Owner: Marcus Liu)
    - In-scope: dynamic batching algorithm, kernel heuristics, regression harness
    - Out-of-scope: console cost UI changes (tracked separately PM-7357)
    - Success metrics: -25% median cost-per-token on production workloads; no increase in P95 latency > 5%
    - Dependencies: ENG-2100 (KV cache persistence), RH-PR-124 (quantization tools)

RACI & Decision Rules:
- R (Responsible): Team owning delivery (usually Engineering Lead)
- A (Accountable): Product Manager for initiative
- C (Consulted): Design, Security, SRE as required
- I (Informed): Stakeholder list (Growth, Sales, Enterprise Success)

Cycle Alignment Process (recommended cadence):
1) T-5 weeks: PMs collect candidate initiatives and fill Initiative Boundary template.
2) T-4 weeks: Cross-functional dependency workshop (mandatory) to populate Dependency Grid.
3) T-3 weeks: Leadership review: map initiatives to company OKRs and rebalance resourcing.
4) T-2 weeks: Finalize planned initiatives and publish the Integrated OKR Map.
5) T+4 weeks (mid-cycle check): Run a health check and consider "rebind" for blocked initiatives.

Dependency Grid fields: initiative_key, owner, dependent_on, dependency_type (blocking/non-blocking), mitigation, target_resolution_date, escalation_contact.

Tooling & Integration:
- Canonical Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.internal/company/okr/integrated-map (master copy)
- Reference spreadsheet (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-okr-integrated-map
- Github implementation tracker example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1245
- Dashboard templates: console.redwood.internal/dashboards/okrs/cost-and-latency

Acceptance & Exit Criteria for marking initiative "Done" in cycle:
- All in-scope items implemented or intentionally deferred in Initiative Boundary with approval.
- Success metrics meet target or runbook is created for follow-up remediation.
- Observability dashboards and alerting live in the console.
- Post-mortem scheduled for partial completions or regressions.

Open decisions (to resolve before publishing playbook):
- Should we allow initiatives to span multiple cycles or require rebind as new initiative? (Proposal: prefer new initiative key for multi-cycle work; allow an explicit "carry" flag with documented scope.)
- How strict is the cost of change gating for C-suite signoff? (Proposal: only for initiatives that alter pricing or SLAs.)

Example initiative mappings (short):
- OBJ-1: "Optimize inference economics" -> ENG-2062, PM-743 (batching), ENG-2199 (config profiles), DES-317 (cost-aware UX)
- OBJ-2: "Enterprise-ready private deployments" -> PM-812 (private onboarding flow), ENG-2330 (VPC control plane), SEC-42 (KMS integration)
- OBJ-3: "Improve developer velocity for inference" -> PM-628 (SDK ergonomics), ENG-2401 (streaming stability), DES-401 (quickstarts)

Communication plan:
- Publish playbook and Integrated OKR Map in Confluence and slack #company-strategy channel.
- Host a 60-minute cross-functional alignment review once map is published (recording saved).

Post-publish governance (how to handle mid-cycle changes):
- Any new initiative that claims >2 FTEs or >3 sprints must be reviewed by the triage board (PM leads + Eng leads).
- Blocking dependency older than 4 weeks triggers immediate escalation to the PM/Eng on record and a weekly unblock report.

Metrics for measuring playbook impact (to be tracked next two cycles):
- Percent of initiatives with completed Initiative Boundary at T-3 weeks (target 95%)
- Reduction in cross-team cycle blockers measured at mid-cycle (target 40% drop)
- Time-to-decision for dependency escalations (target <48 hours)

Next steps:
- Marcus to pilot the template with 3 initiatives this cycle (assigned list in comments).
- Priya to create Confluence template and spreadsheet snapshot (link above).
- Schedule dependency workshop (T-4 weeks) and invite required leads.

Notes & references: Archived OKR mappings from prior cycles (see PM-4821 / PM-6347) for historical context.

2025-11-07 — Anika Rao (SRE): Noted that any initiative touching cache persistence must include a rollback plan and DB migration window. Filed ENG-2100 as dependency and flagged possible 2-week freeze.
